gloss.grammar_note: Infinitive 'rahanā' with negative particle 'nahīṁ' functions as an impersonal deontic modal construction ('one must not dwell').

draft.literal_english: One must not dwell in this land

source.source_text: रहना नहीं इस देस में, देस ये वीराना है
source.roman: rahanā nahīṁ isa desa meṁ, desa ye vīrānā hai

gloss.grammar_note: Two coordinate clauses: first clause is an impersonal modal prohibition ('rahanā nahīṁ isa desa meṁ'), second is a copular clause ('desa ye vīrānā hai') with postnominal demonstrative 'ye' for poetic emphasis.

draft.literal_english: One must not dwell in this land, this land is a desolate wilderness

before.source_text: रहना नहीं इस देस में, देस ये वीराना है
before.roman: rahanā nahīṁ isa desa meṁ, desa ye vīrānā hai

gloss.grammar_note: Copular clause with subject 'desa', postposed demonstrative pronoun 'ye', predicate adjective/noun 'vīrānā', and present copula 'hai'.

draft.literal_english: This land is a desolate wilderness

word_glosses.gloss: world; worldly existence, here portrayed as fragile and perishable

gloss.grammar_note: Equational nominal sentence with elided copula. The genitive postposition 'kī' agrees in feminine gender with 'puṛiyā'.

draft.literal_english: This world is a packet of paper

gloss.grammar_note: 'būnda paṛē' is an oblique/absolutive participial construction serving as a conditional time clause ('upon a drop falling'). 'ḍhala jānā' is an intransitive telic compound verb (ḍhalnā + jānā); combined with 'hai', it expresses inevitable certainty.

draft.literal_english: Upon a drop falling, it is bound to dissolve

word_glosses.gloss: world; worldly existence, here portrayed as fragile and perishable
thicket of thorny bushes and dry scrub

gloss.grammar_note: Equational nominal sentence with elided copula. 'jhāṛō-jhīṅkhara' is an echo-compound / dvandva denoting thorny, desiccated brushwood.

draft.literal_english: This world is a thicket of thorny bushes

gloss.grammar_note: 'āga lagē' is an absolutive/oblique construction functioning as a conditional clause ('upon fire catching'). 'jala jānā' is a completive compound verb (jalnā + jānā) with auxiliary 'hai' conveying destined outcome.

draft.literal_english: Upon fire catching, it is bound to burn down

gloss.grammar_note: Imperfective participle 'kahata' functions as present indicative ('Kabir says'). 'sunō' is 2nd-person plural imperative governing the vocative phrase 'bhāī sādhō'.

draft.literal_english: Says Kabīr, listen, O brother seekers

gloss.grammar_note: Attributive nominal compound 'sataguru nāma' ('the Satguru's Name') functions as subject; 'ṭhikānā' is predicate noun; 'hai' is present copula.

draft.literal_english: The true Guru's Name is the true refuge
